notes:
Lead contact: CTO (Ravi Shah) + Head of Support (Maria Gomez).

Background: National telehealth & billing provider; handles PHI and card payments in chat flows. Mature contact center (Genesys), 500+ concurrent agents at peak, expected to grow. Currently evaluating options to replace brittle in-house LLM proxy used for quick replies and payment routing.

Recent timeline: 
- 2025-11-18: Intro call (Maya) - high level requirements, asked for private deployment options.
- 2025-12-02: Security questionnaire submitted (20 pages) — waiting legal clarifications.

- 2026-03-04: Live demo of agent assist + tool-calling prototype; tested payment redaction flow (ff_20260304_demo).

Requirements / constraints (customer-specified):
- Data residency: primary US regions only, some state-level storage for payment logs.
- Retention: audit logs & transcripts must be retained for 7 years; easy export for compliance audits.
- SSO: SAML + IdP initiated SSO required for admin console.
- KMS/HSM integration for keys; customer-managed key preferred.
- PCI scope: chat paths that touch card numbers must be isolated and redacted; require attestations for scope reduction.
- PHI: all PHI must be segregated; PoC must show encryption-in-transit and at-rest and tokenization of identifiers.
- Availability: 99.99% during business hours; burst tolerance for 2x baseline concurrent agents (500 -> 1000) with <350ms p95 latency for agent assist.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to trade-off medium increased cost for strong guarantees; target ARR band noted above.

Technical preferences:
- Prefer model routing/fallback: high-quality LLM (open) for agent assist + smaller quantized models for simple templated replies.
- KV/prefix caching to reduce cost on repetitive triage.
- Tool-calling: need secure connector to CRM (in-house) for ticket linking; strict audit trail of calls.
- Observability: token-level cost and per-route latency breakdown required for chargeback.

Quotes / paraphrases: 
- CTO: "We cannot risk PHI leakage; show us the keys on day one."
- Head of Support: "Agent productivity gains must be measurable within 30 days of PoC — show summary + time-saved metric."

PoC scope suggested:
- Phase 1: VPC private control plane + secure peering, SAML login, KMS integration, basic agent-assist flow (100 agents).
- Phase 2: Spike testing to 1000 concurrent agents, payment redaction flow, retention & audit export test.
- Acceptance: pass security checklist, meet latency SLOs, exportable audit logs, legal sign-off.

Open items / asks for Redwood:
- Provide network diagram template for VPC peering and private endpoints.
- Fill PCI scoping worksheet and indicate which components will be in-scope.
- Confirm KMS/HSM vendor compatibility and key rotation process.
- Provide sample retention/export scripts and SLAs around log export speed.

Sales notes: 
- High propensity to sign if PoC demonstrates secure redaction + stable latency under spikes.
- Competitive risk: Genesys + in-house ML; emphasis on lower operational burden + observability could win.
